html:
The Sugpiaq, also called Alutiiq, are an Alaska Native people of the Kodiak islands, the Alaska Peninsula, the Kenai coast and Prince William Sound. The map spells their name "Suspiaq". Their language belongs to the Yupik branch of the Eskimo-Aleut family, and they are close kin of the Yupik to the north.

They lived from the sea. Hunters went after seals, sea lions, whales and sea otters in skin kayaks, and salmon runs fed whole villages through the winter.

Russian fur traders arrived in the 1780s. In 1784 Grigory Shelikhov set up a post on Kodiak after his men attacked a Sugpiaq refuge rock and killed many people. The Russian-American Company then forced Sugpiaq men to hunt sea otters for the fur trade, and epidemics cut their numbers sharply. Their neighbours to the east were the Eyaq. After the sale of Alaska in 1867 they came under United States rule, and many still follow the Orthodox Christianity that came with Russian America.
